newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady, interbank rate falls late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady, interbank rate falls late.

text.p: The Thai baht was steady against the dollar in late trade on Tuesday as the U.S unit's rise in Thailand was limited by persistent selling, dealers said.
They said the steady inflow of foreign funds and profit taking on the dollar's recent surge triggered more selling of the dollar against the baht.
The baht was quoted at 25.725-25.730 to the dollar late compared with 25.720-25.730 in morning trade, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.74, the lowest level in more than five years, against 25.71 on Monday.
"The selling of the dollar continued to emerge today. This stemmed the dollar's rise against the baht," one dealer at a foreign bank said.

The overnight interbank rate fell sharply in late trade due to slower demand for funds as most banks appeared to have enough money to meet the central bank's reserve deadline on Wednesday, dealers said.
The heavy selling of the dollar and steady foreign inflows also helped raise market liquidity, dealers said.
The baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 8.50/9.00 satangs per dollar late, unchanged from the morning.
The overnight interbank rate dropped to 8.50 percent near the close from 12.00-12.50 percent in the morning and late on Monday, dealers said.
"There was very high liquidity in the afternoon as most banks tried to lend their surplus cash into the market. All banks appeared to maintain sufficient funds for the reserve," another dealer said.
All commercial banks have to meet the central bank's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of every month.
